confirmedFindings: The packet identifies 32 affected baseline items. All 41 baseline items were reconciled: 2 artifact/not_applicable, 10 missing_from_source/accurately_unavailable, 9 variant_match/accurately_unavailable, 12 variant_match/mismatch, and 8 exact_match/mismatch.

The official menu index exposes six named menu surfaces and explicitly warns that plat du jour and weekend specials may be unlisted. Consequently, source absence cannot establish removals, a complete current catalog, allergen negatives, or cross-contact conclusions.

The restaurant directly links the Toast catalog. Toast currently shows 23 presentations representing 20 unique products; its descriptions are restaurant_linked_vendor evidence and support only narrow explicit or unavoidable positive ingredients, not complete allergen arrays or negatives.

Baseline rows sourced from Toast are improperly classified as official-ingredients. Their valid explicit positives should be retained while their authority is downgraded to restaurant_linked_vendor and their arrays remain partial-positive-only.
The Dinner. Steak Frites presentation is a normalized duplicate of Steak Frites, not Salade Maison. Terra correctly identified the upstream reconciliation error.
No reopened source supplies shared-equipment, fryer, may-contain, or other cross-contact language.

The multi-service, PDF/image, non-exact-reconciliation, parser/repair, low-completeness, and scout-risk gates appropriately required strong review. Count drift is a valid screening signal only; it does not prove product removal because the accessible Toast catalog is not exhaustive.
rejectedFindings: Reject any blanket conclusion that official PDF-derived ingredient evidence lacks restaurant-issued authority merely because the PDFs could not be extracted during this review. The official menu index establishes that the linked PDFs are restaurant-issued; extraction failure prevents revalidation of their contents but does not automatically downgrade their authority.

Reject the deterministic duplicatePresentationCount of 20 as an evidence-backed duplicate count. The reopened Toast page shows three repeated presentations—Bistro Burger, Salade Maison, and Steak Frites—across 23 presentations and 20 unique products.

Reject the deterministic crossContactCount of 2 as substantiated evidence. No affected baseline item or adjudicated group in the packet carries may-contain evidence, and the primary sources disclose no cross-contact condition.
Reject using Terra's low overall confidence to weaken the discrepancy outcome. Menu completeness remains uncertain, but the source-authority and reconciliation discrepancies are directly verifiable.

Reject both wholesale deletion of explicit positive allergens and promotion of culinary expectations into complete arrays. Named cheese, fish, shellfish, nuts, eggs, buns, breadcrumbs, croutons, butter, and pasta support narrow positives where explicitly presented; nothing supports negatives or cross-contact claims.
